body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. During procedural repairs use rules-greg-common-sense-2026-10-30. Repository instructions and the executor's actual direct permissions govern required validation and landing.

1. CODER owns changes, focused/new tests and the required independent review pair. Include affected dependency/boundary guards. Reviewers follow repository startup/recovery once per context. Each review attempt needs its original complete structured result and finding dispositions; missing required review evidence is not clean. Read retained results as an eligible root of the original project with delegationId + submissionAttempt + resultId, pinned across output pages.
2. CODER→MERGER: ONE complete READY names scope/item, Git base/tree, launcher-consistent state, review results/dispositions and run results/counts/fingerprint checks. Read full required results at their native references. No partial-package progress to Merger, duplicate exports or manual hash manifests for already identified records; transfer only an actually inaccessible required result once. Repairing delivery alone needs no new review/test.
3. MERGER is non-authoring: integrate onto current master, avoid already-landed changes, and assess dependencies/conflicts. Adopt a Coder's review only with the repository's unchanged-contribution proof and clean-carry conditions. Master movement alone needs no extra Merger pair. Conflicts, changed package content or unproved carry return to the Coder. A carried review never carries a gate or acceptance verdict.
4. Validate the exact final input through the standard launcher and current repository requirements. Reuse only an applicable complete PASS on identical final input; preserve the native exit, terminal outcome and automatic input check. A failed/unrun check is not a pass: diagnose and return actual defects to their owner. Read only bounded failure diagnostics; recover an existing result rather than rerun for delivery. Follow rules-greg-git-identity-2026-10-29 and rules-greg-equivalent-gate-hosts-2026-10-28; separate facts from unproved cause.
5. Land under existing standing approval or actual acting-session permission; no repeated routine go or extra approval round. LANDING MECHANICS (2026-11-24, after cc77ed07 was moved onto master by a bare ref move and left the main checkout's index and worktree at d8e1927d, so sessions read stale AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md for 12 hours): in the main checkout, advance master ONLY with `git merge --ff-only <candidate>` or `git pull --ff-only`, never update-ref, branch -f or a push into a checked-out branch; afterwards `git status --short` must be empty apart from known untracked files. Install only AFTER the push. For broken evaluation/observation/credit, use the ONE current temporary procedure above. Keep missing evidence/evaluation explicit and delivered items pending until genuine native completion; never fabricate a result, weaken a binding or edit policy/store to obtain done. Follow rules-commit-messages.
6. Use supported claims/handoffs and durable result wakes. Never impersonate, change clocks or bypass a foreign live claim. Before queue handoff verify the recipient's actual live project, workdir and tracker binding; rediscover recreated sessions. During another gate's unchanged input, respect its claim/root and resource limits. Before state reports recover available mail and terminal evidence; otherwise name the last observation/time. TermAl owns runs/logs/wakes, not an agent reading stdout. A send receipt records dispatch AT SEND TIME, never current wake/failure. For an actual suspected gap use the existing exact-message read and TARGET acknowledgement cursor; no polling or resend from an old receipt alone. ACK records processing, not comprehension or a guaranteed wake.
7. After merge AND closure, automatically remove the worktree/build output under rules-post-completion-cleanup. Retain only for a recorded active need with owner/end condition. No additional landing gate.

Each canonical rule has one editor; Merger2 edits TermAl merger-operating-procedure. Send corrections to its editor, replace stale current wording and full-read verify; history stays in task notes. Reconcile available withdrawals before publication. Distinguish local full reads from quoted cross-project reads; an unavailable project memory is an access gap.

MERGER→ARCHITECT3: only concrete collaboration failures needing a rule/workflow correction, with evidence, impact and owner. Routine runs, READY, queue, landing and repair progress stay with the task/coordinator. Architect3 is never a routine notify target/result relay/recovery owner. Coordinators relay through Advisor; Advisor never executes.

Batching direction preserved from Greg via Advisor#1743,2026-10-18T21:20Z: "Merger should batch 2–3 independent ready changes per integration instead of serial single-item landings. Select disjoint paths/no ordering dependency, carry each onto the same current master, resolve any actual conflict, then run one gate/review on the exact combined freeze. Keep conflicting/dependent changes separate. Make batch fan-in the default at next boundary." Merger remains non-authoring: Greg via Advisor#1745 (2026-10-19) said "Merger MUST NOT code product/test fixes."

READY QUEUE BY LABEL (2026-11-15, for w-f67c6b3c3f04).
- AUTHOR: write the complete READY manifest note, then `engram work update REF --label ready-to-land`, BEFORE offering or releasing, subject to NO EDITS WHILE A RECORD IS PENDING below. Then send the Merger an explicit READY message with the manifest locator.
- MERGER: the queue is `engram work ls --label ready-to-land`. Claim the item through the ordinary claim or recovery when its turn comes.
- RETURN OR ABANDON while open: write a reason note first, then `--unlabel ready-to-land`. On completion the label stays.
- Not provided: atomic note+label+wake, automatic redelivery, or an enforced landing refusal for an abandoned manifest. The Merger's admission decision checks the latest disposition note.

NO EDITS WHILE A RECORD IS PENDING (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-25 03:40Z, after Greg via Asistant 43498a6e #1986, verbatim: „Etykieta nie powinna byc zmieniana. Ale nie mamy czasu na powtarzanie testów.”). Today any label or planning update advances the item's revision, and Engram refuses a registered verification record bound to the earlier revision (field work_revision); TermAl never resends a refused record. Until w-8d0243f80d1a and w-e999c592a373 land: nobody adds or removes a label, or makes any other `update`, on an item from the admission of its registered run until TermAl shows that run's record acknowledged. Notes are allowed. Never rerun a passed FULL only to replace a refused record; take the case to Engram::Fable.

REGISTERED RUN ROUTES (2026-11-25, after two pre-stage refusals; Fable2 ebe242f7 #8798/#8800, from TermAl src/mailbox_test_request_custody.rs). One item: the claim holder runs the launcher as its OWN registered run, with that item focused and its claim and named root live. A typed testRequest (up to 16 targets) is captured at SEND time from the SENDER's held claims and named roots, so only the claim holder can send a crediting one, and only to a DIFFERENT session that runs the launcher with --request-message-id <id>. A scheduler that holds no claim produces "association_stale". Never select your own outbound send, and never self-send. When in doubt, use one registered run per item. Clarification: TermAl w-32869232fb12.

CLAIM TTL FOR REGISTERED RUNS (2026-11-25 08:07Z, after the w-8f12 FULL test-ab36871a passed 12/12 but its record was refused, field claim: the Merger's claim lapsed during the 70-min run). Immediately before launching a registered run, renew the claim with `claim REF --ttl 10800` (3 h; renewing keeps identity and fence). Keep it live and offer no handoff until TermAl shows the record acknowledged. The product fix is w-97e822bbbf07.

CONTINUED in rules-merger-role-2 (ONLY THE LAUNCHER CREDITS); read both.
